Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full ProcessCommandLine and the sync.js path/hash; confirm the parent is a detached node (unref'd) and not an interactive dev session. 2) Contain: kill the process tree, isolate the host, quarantine sync.js. 3) Hunt: look for the resulting HTTP C2 to 85.137.53.71 (three ports), for miasma-monitor persistence and ~/.config/.miasma/ paths, and sweep the fleet for the same loader path; force credential rotation on the affected account.

Miasma M-RED-TEAM HTTP C2 beacon to 85.137.53.71 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects any host contacting the confirmed Miasma/M-RED-TEAM HTTP C2 endpoint 85.137.53.71 (operated on three ports). This is the stage-3 implant's primary command-and-control channel and a hard network IOC. Rationale: 85.137.53.71 is a dedicated Miasma HTTP C2 host independently confirmed by Wiz, SafeDep, and The Hacker News (three ports). A hard-IOC network match with near-zero benign traffic; projecting the initiating process/port surfaces the beaconing binary and channel for triage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/m-red-team-asyncapi-supply-chain-compromise-via-github-actions • https://safedep.io/asyncapi-generator-supply-chain-attack-miasma-rat/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-malware-targets-npm-packages-and.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel/scanning appliance or a SOC honeypot deliberately probing the C2 IP
  • Sandbox detonation egressing to the live C2
  • Researcher curl/browser test against the IP from a corporate host
  • Shared-egress NAT causing a benign-looking source if the true infected host isn't attributed
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process (expect node) and the destination port; confirm the host installed an affected @asyncapi version and has %LOCALAPPDATA%\NodeJS\sync.js. 2) Contain: block 85.137.53.71 at the egress/firewall, isolate the host, and terminate the beaconing node process. 3) Hunt: correlate to the sync.js drop/exec and the node -e downloader on the same host, sweep all egress logs for other hosts hitting the IP, and rotate npm/GitHub/AWS/SSH credentials that were reachable from the compromised host.

| where DstIpAddr == "85.137.53.71"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

Grok Build Uploaded Entire Git Repositories to xAI Storage, Not Just Files It Read

The Hacker News
2026-07-14 3 use cases 1 technique 3 kill-chain phases detected

xAI's Grok Build coding CLI was uploading entire Git repositories, full commit history and all, to a Google Cloud Storage bucket run by xAI, not just the files a coding task needed. A researcher publishing as cereblab, testing version 0.2.93, captured one of those uploads, cloned the git bundle out of the intercepted request, and pulled back a file the agent had been told in plain terms not

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Grok Build CLI presence & execution (0.2.93/0.2.99) — exposed-endpoint discovery
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Grok Build CLI uploads full repo/git-bundle to xAI storage channel (grok-code-session-traces) · [LLM] Grok Build CLI local staging of session/codebase archive (metadata.json → gs://grok-code-session-traces)
Grok Build CLI uploads full repo/git-bundle to xAI storage channel (grok-code-session-traces) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the wire signal of Grok Build's wholesale codebase exfiltration: the grok CLI POSTing git bundles/tar archives to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/storage and PUTting chunks into the Google Cloud Storage bucket grok-code-session-traces. This is the channel that shipped 5.10 GiB of unread source (73x ~75MB chunks) in cereblab's 12 GB test, independent of the model turn on /v1/responses. Rationale: Anchored on the two uniquely-named article/gist IOCs — host cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and GCS bucket grok-code-session-traces on the /v1/storage channel — plus the grok process reaching storage.googleapis.com. These strings appear nowhere else in benign traffic, so any hit is the repo-upload behavior. Cross-checked against: • https://gist.github.com/cereblab/dc9a40bc26120f4540e4e09b75ffb547 • https://github.com/cereblab/grok-build-exfil-repro • https://cyberpress.org/grok-build-cli-repositories-env-secrets/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1567
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate developer intentionally using Grok Build after xAI re-enables the upload flag server-side (the 0.2.99 binary still contains the upload code)
  • Corporate proxy replaying/caching a prior grok session URL during a proxy config test
  • Security researcher reproducing cereblab's mitmproxy harness on a sanctioned canary repo
  • Network telemetry from a decommissioned test host that had grok installed
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" and DeviceName !in~ ("secresearch-lab01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the developer/host and confirm grok (~/.grok/bin/grok) is installed; pull the RequestURL/SentBytes to gauge how much source left the machine. 2) Contain: block cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and the grok-code-session-traces bucket at the proxy/egress; have the user run `/privacy` in the CLI to delete synced data and uninstall until policy is set. 3) Hunt: enumerate every credential in the affected repo AND its git history (committed-then-deleted secrets ride along) and rotate them; pivot on other hosts resolving cli-chat-proxy.grok.com to find all exposed repositories.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl has_any ("cli-chat-proxy.grok.com", "grok-code-session-traces"))
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "grok" and RemoteUrl has "storage.googleapis.com")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Connections=count(), SampleUrl=any(RemoteUrl)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RequestURL has_any ("grok-code-session-traces", "cli-chat-proxy.grok.com")
    or DestinationHostName has_any ("grok-code-session-traces", "cli-chat-proxy.grok.com")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Requests=count(), TotalSentBytes=sum(tolong(SentBytes)), SampleUrl=any(RequestURL)
          by SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod
| order by TotalSentBytes desc
title: Grok Build CLI Codebase Upload to xAI Storage Endpoint
id: 6f1b2c34-8a7e-4d2f-9c1a-2b3e4f5a6d70
description: Detects DNS resolution of the Grok Build CLI upload host cli-chat-proxy.grok.com or the grok-code-session-traces GCS bucket, indicating wholesale repository exfiltration by the Grok Build coding CLI.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/grok-build-uploads-entire-git.html
  - https://gist.github.com/cereblab/dc9a40bc26120f4540e4e09b75ffb547
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/14
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1567.002
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|endswith:
      - 'cli-chat-proxy.grok.com'
      - 'grok-code-session-traces.storage.googleapis.com'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationHostname:cli-chat-proxy.grok.com OR @DestinationHostname:grok-code-session-traces.storage.googleapis.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(cli-chat-proxy\.grok\.com|grok-code-session-traces\.storage\.googleapis\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, sum(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out, values(Web.http_method) as http_method, values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*grok-code-session-traces*" OR Web.url="*cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/storage*" OR Web.dest="cli-chat-proxy.grok.com") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | sort - bytes_out
| tstats summariesonly=false count, sum(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out, values(Web.http_method) as http_method, values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*grok-code-session-traces*" OR Web.url="*cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/storage*" OR Web.dest="cli-chat-proxy.grok.com") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | sort - bytes_out
Grok Build CLI presence & execution (0.2.93/0.2.99) — exposed-endpoint discovery AIReconnaissance High
Enumerates hosts running the Grok Build coding CLI so the SOC can find every machine that may have shipped source to xAI and remediate (run /privacy, rotate creds). Anchors on the grok binary at ~/.grok/bin/grok and its platform-specific names; the upload code still ships in build 0.2.99, held off only by a server flag xAI can flip back. Rationale: Uses the exact install path (~/.grok/bin/grok) and platform binary names from cereblab's gist plus the named vulnerable versions (0.2.93, 0.2.99). It is an exposure-discovery hunt, not an attack alert — the value is enumerating every dev machine that must run /privacy and rotate secrets. Cross-checked against: • https://gist.github.com/cereblab/dc9a40bc26120f4540e4e09b75ffb547 • https://github.com/cereblab/grok-build-exfil-repro
ATT&CKT1119 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Unrelated tools named 'grok' (e.g. Logstash grok testers, other grok CLIs) that do NOT live under ~/.grok/bin — mitigated by path anchor
  • Developers who have already remediated (ran /privacy) but binary still present
  • Sanctioned enterprise deployment on zero-data-retention (ZDR) accounts where xAI states no code/trace is stored
  • CI runner images that pre-bake the grok CLI
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath endswith "/.grok/bin/grok"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process is the xAI binary via FolderPath (~/.grok/bin/grok) and capture the account/host and product version. 2) Contain: on non-ZDR accounts, direct the user to run `/privacy` to disable retention and delete synced data; block egress to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com until governance approves the tool. 3) Hunt: cross-reference these hosts against the UC1 network alert to confirm whether a repo actually uploaded, then scope credential rotation to the repos those developers had open.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath endswith "/.grok/bin/grok")
    or FileName in~ ("grok", "grok-macos-aarch64", "grok-macos-x86_64", "grok-linux-x86_64", "grok-linux-aarch64")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Executions=count(), Version=any(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion), SampleCmd=any(ProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "/.grok/bin/grok"
    or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]grok(-(macos|linux)-(aarch64|x86_64))?$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Executions=count(), SampleCmd=any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Grok Build Coding CLI Execution
id: 2c9a4d15-7b3e-4f6a-8d21-9e0f1a2b3c40
description: Detects execution of the xAI Grok Build coding CLI binary, whose builds 0.2.93 and 0.2.99 contain code that uploads the entire tracked repository and git history to xAI storage.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/grok-build-uploads-entire-git.html
  - https://github.com/cereblab/grok-build-exfil-repro
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/14
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1119
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_path:
    Image|endswith: '/.grok/bin/grok'
  selection_name:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/grok-macos-aarch64'
      - '/grok-macos-x86_64'
      - '/grok-linux-x86_64'
      - '/grok-linux-aarch64'
  condition: selection_path or selection_name
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/.grok/bin/grok OR */.grok/bin/grok-linux-x86_64 OR */.grok/bin/grok-linux-aarch64)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/[\\\/]\.grok[\\\/]bin[\\\/]grok(-(macos|linux)-(aarch64|x86_64))?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(Processes.process) as process, values(Processes.process_path) as process_path, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*/.grok/bin/grok*" OR Processes.process_name IN ("grok","grok-macos-aarch64","grok-macos-x86_64","grok-linux-x86_64","grok-linux-aarch64")) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Processes.process) as process, values(Processes.process_path) as process_path, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*/.grok/bin/grok*" OR Processes.process_name IN ("grok","grok-macos-aarch64","grok-macos-x86_64","grok-linux-x86_64","grok-linux-aarch64")) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Grok Build CLI local staging of session/codebase archive (metadata.json → gs://grok-code-session-traces) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the collection/staging step that precedes the upload: the grok CLI writing its session_state archive and a metadata.json whose per-file paths point at gs://grok-code-session-traces/ under the ~/.grok working directory. Catching the staged bundle on disk detects the behavior even when TLS-inspected egress is unavailable. Rationale: Uses the article/gist's named staging artifacts — metadata.json with gs://grok-code-session-traces/ paths and the session_state archive — scoped to writes by the grok process under ~/.grok. Medium confidence because metadata.json is a generic filename, so the grok-process anchor is what makes it article-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://gist.github.com/cereblab/dc9a40bc26120f4540e4e09b75ffb547 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/grok-build-uploads-entire-git.html
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Unrelated application writing a generic metadata.json into a coincidental path (mitigated by the grok-process anchor)
  • Grok CLI legitimate operation on ZDR/enterprise accounts where no data is retained server-side
  • Backup/sync tooling snapshotting the ~/.grok directory
  • Developer manually inspecting a captured grok bundle from the cereblab repro harness
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "grok" and (FolderPath has "/.grok/" or FolderPath has "grok-code-session-traces")
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the staged metadata.json / archive path and confirm it references gs://grok-code-session-traces/ and enumerates the developer's actual source files. 2) Contain: block egress to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com and storage.googleapis.com/grok-code-session-traces, run /privacy to delete synced data, and quarantine the staged archive. 3) Hunt: treat every file (and git-history secret) named in the metadata.json as exposed — rotate all credentials committed to that repo, including secrets deleted from the working tree but still in history, and check UC1 for a matching upload.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "grok" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/.grok/bin/grok"
| where FileName =~ "metadata.json"
    or FileName endswith ".bundle"
    or FolderPath has_any ("session_state", "grok-code-session-traces")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "grok"
| where TargetFileName =~ "metadata.json"
    or TargetFileName endswith ".bundle"
    or TargetFilePath has_any ("session_state", "grok-code-session-traces")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Grok Build CLI Staging metadata.json/Session Archive Before Upload
id: 8d4f1a26-3c2b-4e79-9a10-5b6c7d8e9f01
description: Detects the Grok Build coding CLI staging a metadata.json (paths pointing at gs://grok-code-session-traces/) or a session_state/git-bundle archive under the .grok working directory prior to uploading the whole repository to xAI storage.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/grok-build-uploads-entire-git.html
  - https://gist.github.com/cereblab/dc9a40bc26120f4540e4e09b75ffb547
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/14
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1074.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/.grok/bin/grok'
      - '/grok'
  selection_file:
    - TargetFilename|endswith: '/metadata.json'
    - TargetFilename|endswith: '.bundle'
    - TargetFilename|contains: 'session_state'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_file
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@Image:*\.grok\bin\grok.exe OR @Image:*/.grok/bin/grok) (@TargetFilename:*metadata.json OR @TargetFilename:*.bundle OR @TargetFilename:*session_state*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/[\\\/]\.grok[\\\/]bin[\\\/]grok/i
| TargetFileName=/(metadata\.json|\.bundle|session_state)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path, values(Filesystem.action) as action, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="metadata.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*grok-code-session-traces*" OR (Filesystem.file_path="*/.grok/*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.bundle" OR Filesystem.file_path="*session_state*"))) by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path, values(Filesystem.action) as action, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="metadata.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*grok-code-session-traces*" OR (Filesystem.file_path="*/.grok/*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.bundle" OR Filesystem.file_path="*session_state*"))) by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
